papers.title: Variational Bayesian strategies for high-dimensional, stochastic design problems
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with a lesser-studied problem in the context of model-based, uncertainty quantification (UQ), that of optimization/design/control under uncertainty. The solution of such problems is hindered not only by the usual difficulties encountered in UQ tasks (e.g. the high computational cost of each forward simulation, the large number of random variables) but also by the need to solve a nonlinear optimization problem involving large numbers of design variables and potentially constraints. We propose a framework that is suitable for a large class of such problems and is based on the idea of recasting them as probabilistic inference tasks. To that end, we propose a Variational Bayesian (VB) formulation and an iterative VB-Expectation-Maximization scheme that is also capable of identifying a low-dimensional set of directions in the design space, along which, the objective exhibits the largest sensitivity.   We demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach in the context of two numerical examples involving $\mathcal{O}(10^3)$ random and design variables. In all cases considered the cost of the computations in terms of calls to the forward model was of the order $\mathcal{O}(10^2)$. The accuracy of the approximations provided is assessed by appropriate information-theoretic metrics.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的变分贝叶斯方法可用于高维设计优化与不确定性量化，可迁移至植入物设计中的代理模型与优化问题。
llm.why_not_core: No application to biomechanics or implant design, no explicit constraint handling, and validation only on synthetic numerical examples without real-world FEA simulations.

summary_zh.motivation: 针对高维随机设计问题中的不确定性量化与优化效率低下问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出变分贝叶斯期望最大化框架，将优化问题转化为概率推断。
summary_zh.result: 在数千维变量下仅需约100次前向调用即可获得准确近似。
summary_zh.validation: 在数值基准例中使用信息论指标验证精度。

summary_en.motivation: To address the computational bottleneck of optimization under uncertainty with high-dimensional random and design variables.
summary_en.method: A Variational Bayesian Expectation-Maximization formulation that recasts design optimization as probabilistic inference.
summary_en.result: Achieves accurate approximations with only O(10^2) forward model calls for problems with O(10^3) variables.
summary_en.validation: Information-theoretic metrics on two high-dimensional numerical benchmarks.
